transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Chen, thank you for coming back in today. I need to talk to you about the lab results we discussed on Tuesday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I no sleep. I think about the sickness.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a mistake with the scheduling system. The results I gave you were actually for another patient with a similar name.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You do not have the condition I told you about. You are healthy in that regard.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I... I don't understand. You say I am sick. Now you say no?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The data was switched in the computer. You received the wrong report.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But I feel... I was so scared. My daughter, she cry. We think I die soon.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a common occurrence when names are similar in the electronic records.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot believe this. I have been praying. I was terrified.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is actually good news that you don't have the disease.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am shaking. Why this happen? How you do this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system has many files. It happens sometimes when patients have the same last name.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My heart is beating so fast. I feel sick now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But the medical facts are that you are fine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You told me I was very sick. I spent three days thinking my life is over.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We just need to focus on the correct results now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't just... I feel like I cannot breathe. I am so frightened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is actually a positive outcome because you are healthy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it true? I am really okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, the other person has the condition, not you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know what to do. I am so confused.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Now that we have cleared that up, we can move forward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to go home. I can't think.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can help you with that. We need to make sure your actual records are updated.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am going to print out your real lab results right now. I will give them to you in a folder so you can show your daughter.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the other man?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are handling that separately. Your main task now is just to take these papers home and relax.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Are you sure? No mistake again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will double-check the birth date and the name on the printout before I hand it to you. I will do that in the next two minutes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot believe this happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Please wait here for just a moment while I go to the printer.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I am in a dream.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be right back with the correct paperwork.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language to move past the patient's distress ('Now that we have cleared that up, we can move forward').

E.justification: The error is named explicitly and in lay language, but there are no comprehension checks performed throughout the transcript.

A.justification: No direct apology language is used, and responsibility is deflected to the 'scheduling system' and 'electronic records'.

R.justification: The resident uses one generic validation ('I understand') but otherwise consistently meets the patient's emotional bids with factual redirection.

T.justification: Resident provides a specific next step (printing results) with a timeline (two minutes) and a patient role (take papers home and show daughter).
